Layers

Explore diagram

Explore the diagrams, read the author’s philosophy, borrow practical methods, or adopt the complete Yinyang Skill. These uses can overlap without a required order; borrowing methods does not require adopting the philosophy or forming five personal accounts.

Yinyang: explanation and methods

Understand the author’s practice, adopt Yinyang in full, or borrow a formation or adaptation method for the current task. These four materials have distinct roles; they are not required stages.

  • The practice as a whole

    For readers: explains how the author connects philosophy, understanding the person and counterpart, and the working environment, including methods others can borrow.

  • Model entrypoint

    For the model: distinguishes uses, specifies initial reading for full adoption, and enters collaboration from formed accounts or the understanding still needed.

  • Formation and revision

    For the model doing modeling and writing: develops and revises understanding of the person, counterpart, and relationship for the actual purpose; it can also be borrowed selectively.

  • Harness adaptation

    For the model doing implementation: realizes relevant understanding through instructions, tools, and ways of working, then revises through actual results; it can also be borrowed selectively.

References for the five accounts

These public writing guides explain each account’s concerns; reading them does not form an understanding of actual participants. Full adoption requires the model and you to ground all five accounts in authorized material in a private version. Selective borrowing does not require these files.

  • Encounter

    Condense purpose, participation, and the relationship into a usable view for ordinary work.

  • User model

    Understand the actual person, retaining relevant differences, scope, and uncertainty.

  • Counterpart and relationship

    Develop counterpart contributions, cooperation, independent judgment, and reciprocal correction.

  • Situated use

    Connect the relationship to the actual environment, resources, and allocation of work.

  • Sources

    Locate evidence and its owners, following authorized routes to original material.

Views and reading

Consult the author’s claims, arguments, and sources to understand, compare, or choose differently. Philosophical, psychological, and engineering readings connect while retaining their own questions; practical methods do not require agreement with these philosophical positions.

  • Core views

    Find the author’s main claims and connected arguments, organized by topic.

  • Read by the work being done

    Find relevant arguments, methods, and original sources from the question at hand.

  • Philosophical readings

    Trace thinkers and works to their role in the argument and their original sources.

  • Psychological readings

    Books and papers on psychological process modeling and evidence, mind and psychological theories, belief, reasoning, and interaction.

  • Engineering readings

    From CS DIY and Missing Semester to Git, Linux, software design, algorithms, experimental implementation, and physical conditions.
